## The edit loop

A long-running Rust server watches the file, re-renders on save, and pushes only
what changed over a websocket.

::: {.feature-grid}
::: {.feature}
### Live preview
Open it in any browser. The server watches the `.qmd` (and its includes and
bibliography) and re-renders the moment you save.
:::

::: {.feature}
### Block-level diffing
Each save diffs the new blocks against the old and ships only the differences.
Unchanged blocks are never touched; scroll, focus, and live state survive.
:::

::: {.feature}
### Click to source
Double-click any rendered element and your editor jumps to the line it came from,
even across `{{< include >}}`d files.
:::

::: {.feature}
### Warm kernel
A persistent Jupyter kernel (Python or R) runs your cells. A code change re-runs
only the earliest changed cell and everything downstream, never the whole document.
:::

::: {.feature}
### Preview on your phone
`--host` exposes the live preview on your LAN with a QR code, so you can read the
real, updating page on a phone while you write.
:::

::: {.feature}
### No runaway cells
A cell that runs too long is interrupted, and kernel failures surface in seconds
with the real cause; the warm kernel and prior cells survive.
:::
:::

## Everything technical writing needs

Math, diagrams, runnable code, citations: all rendered offline, all part of the
block model.

::: {.feature-grid}
::: {.feature}
### Math, offline
KaTeX renders inline and display math server-side. Fonts and CSS are bundled, so
equations need no network and never reflow on load.
:::

::: {.feature}
### Diagrams
Mermaid flowcharts, sequence, and state diagrams from fenced code, re-themed
automatically when you toggle light and dark.
:::

::: {.feature}
### Executable code
Python and R cells run against the warm kernel; their output (text and matplotlib
figures alike) is spliced back into the page as real blocks.
:::

::: {.feature}
### Citations & cross-refs
`[@key]` citations with IEEE/CSL bibliographies, and `@fig-` / `@sec-`
cross-references that number and link themselves across chapters.
:::

::: {.feature}
### Numbered figures
Figures get automatic numbering and captions, callouts and columns come from fenced
divs, and `{{< include >}}` stitches files together.
:::

::: {.feature}
### Cmd-K search
A keyboard-driven palette searches every page or chapter. Front-matter typos are
flagged as you write, before they bite.
:::
:::

## Live, and it stays alive

Interactive graphics keep their runtime state across edits, because the page never
reloads.

::: {.feature-grid}
::: {.feature}
### Observable reactivity
Observable JS cells give you sliders and reactive figures. Edit a value and the
reactive graph recomputes live, in place.
:::

::: {.feature}
### 3D graphics
Drop in a Three.js / WebGL canvas. Edit the prose around it and the canvas keeps
spinning; its WebGL context is never torn down.
:::

::: {.feature}
### Code that runs on slides
The same executable cells work in a deck. Edit a `{python}` cell mid-talk and the
slide updates in place. No other framework does this.
:::
:::

## Offline-first, and self-contained

No CDN, no build pipeline. `build` writes HTML you can host anywhere.

::: {.feature-grid}
::: {.feature}
### Zero CDN
Fonts, KaTeX, syntax highlighting, and the slide engine are all bundled. Pages
render identically offline and never phone home.
:::

::: {.feature}
### Self-contained HTML
One command turns a document into a single HTML file, or a portable folder with
its local assets copied alongside.
:::

::: {.feature}
### Whole sites
Point it at a directory and the same engine builds a multi-page website or book to a
static `_site/` you can host anywhere. See [the document types](formats.qmd#websites)
for what each output gives you.
:::
:::
